persona: Film-loving, design-literate visitor who enjoys cinematic, game-like sites and hates gimmicks
inputs: reader-1440 sheets-panel 01–13, reader-1024 sheets-panel 01–12, clips-panel.json (both), scenes/1440 sheets 01–08 (static context)

screens.why: The cold open earns its 14 s: candles, a broom pushing in over Hogwarts, a hard cut to the glowing sea, then the blackletter name card. It plays like a teaser, not a loading screen.
The porthole irises open onto the Black Pearl, with a gold rim, a held frame and 'The Crossing' ghosting in. Best reveal on the page.
The 'A research journal in four acts' contents card promises a structure I want to see through.
The film stops for an essay: three columns of small grey text under the headline. First lull.
Sticky harbour image plus a voyage map. This is scrollytelling that tells me something will change.
The sky changes (harbour to storm) as I read. The left column is mostly empty, but the image carries the screen.
Moon, then bioluminescence, then dawn, while the map nodes tick on. A small montage that pays off.
Arrival at sunset, then a clean act break into '3 Idiots' over a glowing sea strip.
The night sea wipes into a sunlit lecture hall and the chalk drone draws itself. A real match cut.
The 'The Workshop' letter mask lands the first time. The pen slides in, with an odd dark gap.
'Led by what survived scrutiny.', then about 4 s of a static frame with two-thirds of it empty. Dead air.
Seven bars chalked on a blackboard in a shaft of light: a clever way to show the gauntlet.
The case file opens with a corridor image and a 'Rancho' blueprint that draws itself.
The blueprint resolves and a hand-drawn circle flags the key stat. A human touch.
Chalk writes 'What is a machine?' on its own. A lovely beat before the second case.
The second case file is a re-shoot of the first: same layout, same lecture-hall crop, same blueprint. Seen it.
Stats again over the same corridor image. Small text, nothing new.
'See the thesis, not just read it' and a chart that grows: it promises I can play. The style turns into a generic dashboard, though.
A real photo of his drone breaks the AI-render spell in a good way, and there is a button on it.
'What I can actually do.' becomes a skills matrix in tiny type. Résumé, not film.
More matrix and a long vertical blueprint. Static.
'The kill-list' is an honest, intriguing idea, and the mini-blueprint marker sliding down the list is a nice touch.
Six-plus seconds of a long, dim list of dead strategies. My eyes glaze over.
'Three films and a game' sits in plain sans alone on black. It reads like a missing image, not a title card.
The Pirates card, with a compass overlay and 'Not all treasure is silver and gold, mate.' It is the same ship for the third time, though.
A hard colour change to the yellow scooter at Pangong Lake. A breath of fresh air.
'Aal izz well.', then the blood-red RDR2 plain. Each film gets its own palette and type.
'Be loyal to what matters.', then a quill writes 'HARRY POTTER'. Brisk and playful.
The Hogwarts Express on the viaduct, with a golden snitch darting past. I want to catch it.
A framed sepia photograph slowly develops. A gorgeous idea, though showing RDR2 again right after its card is confusing.
A long hold on the sunset, then the third giant-letter mask, whose middle frame goes almost black. Repetition.
'Discipline, service, and a trained eye.' over full-bleed golden hour: the poster shot of the page.
A hand-drawn trail map on parchment. It feels like Arthur's journal.
The same sunset is reused as a sticky side image beside small text columns. Fourth time I have seen it.
Still the sunset, but 'What's in the satchel' appears and I want to open it.
Inventory icons and a WANTED poster with his name. Pure game, perfectly in-world.
The page lifts like paper into Arthur Morgan's journal, and its sketches draw themselves.
'Thinking in public, soon.' is a list of posts that do not exist yet, with faint sketches. Nothing to read.
More unwritten entries, then a muddy cream-to-black smear.
'In their words.' over the gang's camp at dusk: warm, with real people vouching for him.
Tiny italic quotes over a darkening image, then a 'HARRY POTTER' header over an RDR2 campfire. Confusing.
A ring burns through the campfire, a golden light streaks across and the Great Hall appears. The best cut on the page.
The fourth letter mask ('The Light'), then the hall skews and a blank cream box rises. Seen it, and it looks unloaded.
The Marauder's map: footprints walk and a quill writes 'A small philosophy of work.' Delightful.
Five identical principle cards with the same footprints. The gag wears out, and the capture stutters at about 5 fps.
The map gives way to floating candles and 'Let's talk research…'. A classy turn to the ask.
A clear contact block, then an end-credits crawl begins. A film lover's grin.
I stay for a post-credits scene, even though the crawl's type is tiny and dim.
'Mischief managed.' The wink rewards staying to the end.
The same cold open, and the name card fits 1024 well. The broom flips vertical for a frame.
The porthole iris into the Black Pearl still lands.
'The Crossing' ghost title over the ship, then the four-act contents. A clear promise.
About: three columns of small serif text, cramped at 1024. A lull.
Still the wall of text around the compass emblem.
'How the methodology was earned', with the harbour and the voyage map, pulls me back in.
Storm turns to moonlit glow as I read, and the map ticks on.
A dawn arrival, then '3 IDIOTS' over a storm strip: a clear act break.
A pale cyan cloud eats the sea and fills the frame with a ring in the middle. It looks like an image failing to load.
The lecture hall clears in with the chalk drone, and the 'The Workshop' letter mask reads cleanly here.
The pen on the desk slides in and 'Led by what survived scrutiny' types itself.
A static hold with most of the frame empty.
The chalkboard gauntlet with its light beam, then the first case file starts.
Corridor plus a blueprint drawing itself: a solid case-file opening.
The blueprint branches and resolves, and the stats appear.
A hand-drawn circle on a stat, and the chalk begins 'What is a machine?'.
The second case file, with the same template and the same lecture-hall crop. Seen it.
The second blueprint looks like the first.
Stats again over the same corridor.
The 'See the thesis' card goes full width at 1024, and the growing chart invites a poke.
The chart scrolls off and leaves an empty green panel.
A real drone photo, then 'What I can actually do.'
A skills matrix with five cramped columns at 1024. Unreadable at a glance.
The kill-list idea hooks me, though an empty tall outline box sits in the list.
The long dim list continues.
More list. The section overstays.
'Three films and a game' in plain sans on empty black. The ship only arrives at the end.
The Pirates card with its compass, then '3 IDI|' types in.
The yellow scooter at Pangong Lake: fresh daylight.
The red RDR2 plain with little Dead Eye target brackets. It invites a shot.
A quote, then a quill writes 'HARRY POTTER'.
The Hogwarts Express, with the snitch zipping past and hovering over the next header.
A framed sepia photo develops into golden hour. Beautiful.
The third letter mask: the frame goes nearly black, then two image strips stack with a gap between them.
'Discipline, service, and a trained eye.' full-bleed.
The trail-map sketch on parchment.
The same sunset again as a side image, beside small mono text.
The satchel appears, and I want to know what is in it.
The WANTED poster rises with his name on it.
The page lifts into the cream journal.
A list of unwritten posts with faint sketches.
Same.
A smeared cream-to-black fade. The camp only arrives at the end.
'In their words.': warm testimonials by the campfire.
Tiny quotes, then a 'HARRY POTTER' header over the RDR2 campfire.
A burn-through portal into the Great Hall. The showpiece.
The fourth letter mask leaves a near-black frame, then a small blank cream box appears.
The Marauder's map, with a quill writing the title.
The first principles, with walking footprints, still charm.
Cards 3 to 5 repeat the same gag.
Contact with floating candles. A clear ask.
The credits crawl. I wait for a post-credits scene, even with the tiny type.
'Mischief managed.'

acts.act: Prologue: play screen, broom flight, the name
acts.feel: A held cold open, about 14 s before the first scroll. Candles, a push-in over Hogwarts, a hard cut to the glowing sea, a title card. The slowness is earned. Only the 2 s on the empty sea (#5 at 1440) is one beat long.

acts.act: Act I: The Crossing (Pirates: ship, contents, about, voyage)
acts.feel: An iris-in reveal, then a talky about scene that stalls, then a short montage of changing skies over a voyage map. Classic first-act rhythm.

acts.act: Act II: The Workshop (3 Idiots: method, gauntlet, two case files)
acts.feel: It opens on a sharp match cut (sea to classroom) and a title mask, then settles into long static case-file holds. The second case file is a re-shoot of the first, on the same sets.

acts.act: Interlude: The Lab (experiment, drone and skills, kill-list)
acts.feel: The edit loses its eye here. A flat dashboard, a skills table and a long dim list. The drone photo and the kill-list idea are the only cuts that wake me.

acts.act: Three films and a game (film cards)
acts.feel: After a weak title card, four film cards play out in about 15 s, each with its own palette and typeface, and a quill and a snitch as transitions. The best-cut sequence on the page.

acts.act: Act III: The Frontier (RDR2: photo, discipline, satchel and wanted poster, journal, voices)
acts.feel: A photo develops, then the golden-hour hero shot. After that it lingers on the same sunset. The satchel and wanted poster are a great gag. The 'soon' journal is a quiet coda that drags, and the campfire voices warm it up again.

acts.act: Act IV: The Light (HP: burn-through to the Great Hall, Marauder's map principles)
acts.feel: The burn-through portal cut is the showpiece. The map is charming, but the five principle cards loop the same footprint gag.
Contact, then a proper end-credits crawl and a post-credits wink. Right for a film, but the crawl is too dim to read.

discovery.thing: Header controls: 'Skip to the research', a wave glyph that reads as sound, Menu

discovery.thing: Four-act contents list (The Crossing to The Light)
discovery.note: As chapter jumps on a return visit.

discovery.thing: Jack's compass emblem (About), and the compass with a needle on the Pirates film card
discovery.note: I would try to spin the needle.

discovery.thing: Voyage route map whose nodes light up as the story moves
discovery.note: Clicking a node to jump would be nice.

discovery.thing: Kill-list mini-blueprint that follows the active row
discovery.note: Hovering rows to see why each idea died.

discovery.thing: 'Three films and a game' title, which promises a game
discovery.note: I went looking for the game and found no signpost to it.

discovery.thing: Golden snitch darting past the Hogwarts Express and over headers
discovery.note: I would chase it at once.

discovery.thing: Dead Eye target brackets on the RDR2 film image

discovery.note: It reads as an RDR2 inventory I can open.

discovery.thing: WANTED poster with Aryan's name and a reply link

discovery.thing: Glowing ring that appears on the campfire image before it burns through

discovery.thing: Marauder's map footprints walking between principles
discovery.note: I would hover and follow them.

discovery.thing: Contact email pill and 'open in your mail app'
End credits and the post-credits 'Mischief managed.'
discovery.note: A reward for staying, not a toy. That is fine.

discovery.thing: Hints of a collectible hunt (ticks on the satchel items, a ring on the scooter in the static scenes)
discovery.note: Only visible in the static scenes. A passive scroll never tells me there is something to find.

findings.finding: Sea-to-classroom wipe: a pale cyan cloud fills the whole image with a small ring in the centre for about 2 s. It reads as an image failing to load, or a spinner, and it is a bright flash on a dark page.

Body copy is small light grey on near-black, often in three columns (About). The same holds for the journey steps (s6–7), case files (s13–17), skills matrix (s20–21), kill-list (s22–23) and testimonials (s41). Hard to read while scrolling.
The skills matrix crams five columns of tiny text at 1024.

The giant-letter mask transition is used four times: The Crossing (s2 #13), The Workshop (s10 #32), The Frontier (s31 #82) and The Light (s42–43 #108–109). Mid-transition frames go nearly black: '…rontier' alone on black, 'The Light' on black (1024 #77 and #102). By the third time it is a tic.

A 'HARRY POTTER' header sits over an RDR2 campfire image captioned 'The campfire · Red Dead Redemption 2' for about 3 s before the burn transition, so the label and the picture disagree. The same happens at 1024 s45–46 (#98–100).
Kill-list: an empty tall outline rectangle sits beside the first row and looks like a broken image until it becomes the mini-blueprint. The same at 1024 s24 (#57–59).
A small blank cream rectangle rises from black before it unfolds into the Marauder's map, and it reads as an unloaded placeholder. The same at 1024 s47 (#103).

During scene changes, two image strips stack with a dark gap between them (lecture hall above, pen below), which looks like a layout glitch. It recurs at s32 #83 (sunset), 1024 s11 #30 and 1024 s34 #77.
Dead area: 'Led by what survived scrutiny' and a short paragraph, with the right two-thirds empty and the frame static for about 4 s. The same at 1024 s12.
The 'Three films and a game' title card is small plain sans alone on black, so it looks as if an image failed to appear. The generic type also breaks the per-film typography.

Images are reused heavily. The lecture-hall and corridor renders appear 5+ times across Act II, the Black Pearl 3 times (hero, s2, s25), the golden-hour sunset 4 times (s31–35) and the astronaut pen 3 times (s10, s22). This wears down the feeling of a new scene.
The experiment switches to generic sans and a flat dashboard card, with the right third empty. A tonal break from the chalk-and-film look.
The broom flips vertical for a frame (#2 f4; 1024 #2 f3–4), and the outgoing caption 'A broomstick over Hogwarts' overlaps the incoming 'Toward the Black Pearl' (#4 f1; 1024 #3 f4).
The 'THE FRONTIER' ghost title overlaps the 'Golden hour in the Heartlands' caption under the framed photo.
RDR2 appears twice back to back (the film card at s27–28, then the Act III header at s30), and for a moment I thought I had scrolled back.
The 'The Crossing' title ghosts over the ship at large size and reads as a double exposure or text bleed (1024 #13 too).
In the journal every entry is 'soon', the sketches are very faint on cream, and the section ends in a smeared cream-to-black band (#99 f3–4, #100 f1; 1024 #93–94).
A dark strip with the 'Red Dead Redemption 2' label sits above the cream journal page, like a header that did not release.
The credits crawl is microscopic and dim on black for about 10 s.
On the principle cards the capture frame rate falls to about 5 fps (1024 #108–110 to about 6–8), so the map may stutter. I could not confirm this from the stills.
The ship image is cropped to a thin band at the top while a dim ship silhouette sits behind the contents list. Muddy.
Two seconds of near-identical dark sea before the name. One beat too long.

scoreNotes.keepScrolling: About two-thirds yes. The prologue, film cards and finale hold me completely. Act II's second case file, the Lab and the 'soon' journal are where I would start skimming.
scoreNotes.tempo: The open, the film cards and the HP portal are edited like a film. The middle sags on 4–8 s static holds, repeated sets and a transition trick used four times.
scoreNotes.discovery: Lovely toys (snitch, satchel, WANTED poster, Dead Eye brackets, compass, the thesis chart), but they cluster after minute 2 and nothing signals they are playable. The promised 'game' has no signpost.
